assumptions.allowance: Synthetic. A capacity-1 account has 500 units per five-hour window and 5000 per weekly window; capacity scales both linearly. Real allowances are not published.
assumptions.windows: Synthetic. Five-hour and weekly windows reset on a fixed schedule from the fixture start; real five-hour windows start at first use.
assumptions.cost: Synthetic. One unit is 1000 weighted tokens: uncached input 1, cache write 1.25, cache read 0.1, output 5. These are API price ratios, used only as a stand-in for allowance consumption.
assumptions.cache: Synthetic. A prompt prefix stays cached for 5 minutes after its last use, per account and conversation. A request on another account while the old cache is warm counts its prefix as a migration write.
assumptions.observations: Every response reports exact utilization and resets, except acct-e, whose responses carry no quota headers.
assumptions.external_load: acct-c loses 10% of its five-hour allowance per hour to clients outside this proxy.
assumptions.overage: A settings read finds paid overflow disabled on every account every 15 minutes, except acct-d between hours 4 and 8: a response shows paid use at hour 4, and a check at hour 8 finds overflow disabled again.
assumptions.faults: 2% transient failures before output, 1% partial streams, 1% cancellations; acct-b logs out at hour 20 and logs in again at hour 26, and stalled conversations move manually after 30 minutes; the proxy restarts at hours 12, 21, and 30. The restart at hour 21 loses the logout, so new conversations placed on acct-b fail their first request.
